answer_summary: The exact number is 3: L has two distinguishable choices for which of its unit-1/unit-4 primary OH sites becomes the tether, and an unordered pair of the resulting two monomer end types gives AA, AB = BA, and BB.
assumptions: The first primary OH is normalized as unit 1 and the stated directing rule selects the available unit 4 as the second free primary site of L.
As displayed in the product scheme, exactly one of those two primary sites on each beta-CD end bears the tether and the other remains CH2OH.
The alpha-1,4-linked seven-unit ring has an oriented cyclic constitution, so tether-at-unit-1 and tether-at-unit-4 are distinct regioforms.
Swapping the two identical beta-CD ends across the symmetric hydrogenated spacer does not define a new constitutional isomer.
